### The SMB Verification Dilemma


If you run a small or mid-size business in India, you have probably asked yourself: should we verify employees ourselves, or should we hire a background verification company?


The traditional answer has been binary. Either you do it in-house (photocopying IDs, calling previous employers, manually checking documents) or you outsource it to a third-party BGV company (AuthBridge, SpringVerify, HireRight) that charges Rs. 1,500 to Rs. 5,000+ per candidate with annual contracts and sales-led onboarding.


But in 2026, there is a third option that most SMBs do not know about: **self-serve verification tools** that give you the speed of in-house and the accuracy of third-party, without the limitations of either.


The data makes this decision urgent. AuthBridge’s Workforce Fraud Files H1 FY26 found that **4.33% of white-collar candidates carry at least one discrepancy** . HireRight’s 2026 India benchmark reported that **74% of Indian employers detected identity fraud** during screening. And EY’s study found that **85% of discrepancies were caught through employment verification** , the exact check most SMBs skip because they cannot afford a third-party BGV company.


This guide compares all three approaches, in-house, third-party, and self-serve, on cost, speed, accuracy, compliance, and ease of use, so you can choose the right approach for your business.


### What In-House Verification Actually Means


When an SMB does verification in-house, here is what that typically involves:

Call previous employer Phone call to listed reference number Confirm tenure (if HR responds) Fake numbers, colluding contacts


Google the candidate Search for red flags online Public news articles Nothing behind paywalls; no structured data


Check education certificates Visual inspection of marksheets Obviously forged documents High-quality fakes

### The Fundamental Limitation


In-house verification relies on visual inspection and phone calls to unverified numbers. It cannot query government databases (Income Tax for PAN, EPFO for employment, Vahan/Sarathi for DL). It catches only the most obvious fraud while missing the 4.33% of candidates with discrepancies that look legitimate on paper.

#### Why Government Database Verification Is More Reliable Than Manual Checks


In-house HR teams verify against the candidate’s own submitted documents. The candidate controls the source material. If a candidate submits a fake PAN card, visual inspection cannot detect it.


Third-party BGV companies verify against government databases but also rely on manual processes (calling employers, visiting courts) that introduce human delay and error.


SalaryBox Verify queries government databases directly (Income Tax for PAN, EPFO for employment, Vahan/Sarathi for DL, Election Commission for Voter ID). The candidate cannot fabricate or manipulate government records. This makes self-serve verification more reliable than in-house and equally reliable to third-party for the checks it covers.

#### Why Compliance Matters for SMBs in 2026


The Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 (DPDP) requires all businesses to obtain informed consent before processing personal data, use data only for the stated purpose, and store it securely. An SMB that photocopies PAN cards and files them in an unlocked cabinet is technically non-compliant.


SalaryBox Verify addresses this with consent-based verification flows, masked sensitive data in reports, and a private digital workspace. It is not as comprehensive as enterprise DPDP solutions from AuthBridge or First Advantage, but it is dramatically better than the in-house approach of most SMBs.

If you are hiring someone and paying them Rs. 15,000+ per month, Rs. 499 for verification is 0.03% of their first year’s salary. The real reason SMBs do in-house verification is not budget — it is awareness. They do not know affordable self-serve tools exist.

#### FAQs: In-House vs. Third-Party vs. Self-Serve Verification


###### 1. What is the cheapest way for an SMB to verify employees in India?


SalaryBox Verify at Rs. 499 per candidate is the cheapest option that includes government database verification (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN/EPFO). In-house verification appears free but costs Rs. 360–Rs. 720 per hire in HR time and lacks government database accuracy. Third-party BGV companies charge Rs. 1,500–Rs. 5,000+ per candidate.


###### 2. Can in-house verification catch fake PAN cards?


No. In-house verification relies on visual inspection of the physical PAN card. A well-made fake PAN card looks identical to a genuine one. The only way to catch a fake, inactive, or mismatched PAN is to verify the PAN number against the Income Tax Department database, which SalaryBox Verify and third-party BGV companies do.


###### 3. Do SMBs really need background verification?


Yes. AuthBridge data shows that 4.33% of candidates carry discrepancies regardless of company size. A 50-person SMB hiring 20 people per year will statistically encounter 1 candidate with a discrepancy every year. At Rs. 499 per hire on SalaryBox Verify, the annual verification cost is Rs. 9,980 — far less than the cost of one bad hire.


###### 4. What checks does SalaryBox Verify offer that in-house cannot?


SalaryBox Verify queries government databases that in-house HR teams cannot access: the Income Tax Department for PAN status, the EPFO for employment history, the Election Commission for Voter ID, and Vahan/Sarathi for DL validity. In-house teams can only visually inspect physical documents and make phone calls.


###### 5. Is SalaryBox Verify as comprehensive as AuthBridge?


Yes, SalaryBox Verify offers 4 government database checks (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN/EPFO). However, for most SMB hires, these 4 checks cover the two most common fraud types: identity fraud and fabricated employment.


###### 6. Should I switch from my current BGV company to SalaryBox Verify?


It depends on which checks you actually use. If you are paying Rs. 1,500–Rs. 5,000 per hire for comprehensive screening but most of your hires only need identity and employment verification, switch your standard hires to SalaryBox Verify (Rs. 499) and keep your BGV company for the 10–20% of hires that need criminal or education checks.


###### 7. Can SalaryBox Verify handle the DPDP Act compliance requirement?


SalaryBox Verify provides consent-based verification workflows, masked sensitive data in reports, and digital audit trails. This covers the basic DPDP requirements for candidate data processing. Enterprise BGV companies offer more comprehensive DPDP compliance frameworks, but for most SMBs, SalaryBox Verify’s approach is sufficient.


###### 8. How do I convince my management to invest in verification?


Frame it as risk reduction, not cost. At Rs. 499 per hire, verification costs 0.03% of an employee’s first-year salary (at Rs. 20,000/month). The cost of one bad hire (replacement + lost productivity + potential legal issues) is Rs. 3–5 lakh. Show management the 4.33% discrepancy rate from AuthBridge and calculate the expected number of discrepancies in your annual hiring.


###### 9. Can I use SalaryBox Verify for contract workers and freelancers?


Yes. SalaryBox Verify works for anyone with Indian government-issued documents (PAN, Voter ID, DL). There are no restrictions on employment type. Contract workers and freelancers can be verified the same way as full-time employees, at the same Rs. 499 per candidate.


###### 10. What if I need criminal checks for some hires but not all?


Use the hybrid approach: SalaryBox Verify (Rs. 499) for all hires to cover identity and employment verification, and add SpringVerify (Rs. 799+) or AuthBridge (custom pricing) only for hires that require criminal record screening. This saves Rs. 60,000–67,000 annually for a 50-hire SMB compared to using a third-party BGV company for everyone.
